# Green Codex

> A Codex skill for scoped Green IT and responsible digital practices, with evidence for each assessed finding.

- Maintainer: Institut du Numérique Responsable (INR)
- Repository: https://github.com/Institut-du-Numerique-Responsable/green-codex
- Website: https://institut-du-numerique-responsable.github.io/green-codex/
- Presentation in French: https://institutnr.org/ecoconcevoir-avec-un-assistant-de-code
- Version: see https://github.com/Institut-du-Numerique-Responsable/green-codex/blob/main/VERSION

## Scope

Use the skill for software design, implementation, review and audits, or natural-language requests about responsible digital practices. Select only the rules relevant to the task. A small code change does not require an organisational audit.

The catalogue covers software efficiency, accessibility, data, infrastructure, lifecycle, responsible AI, language-specific practices and responsible use of Codex. It includes the NR charter, BP-AIR, stakeholder maturity and RIA31 adaptations alongside mappings to RGESN, GR491, Opquast and RGAA. Project rule identifiers are not official criterion numbers.

## Verification and closing summary

Assessed findings use PASS, FAIL or REVIEW_REQUIRED with scoped evidence. Missing proof does not establish a violation. Human decisions, training and organisational adoption require external evidence. Passing tests does not certify compliance. RIA31 is distinct from the EU AI regulation.

The skill requests an end-of-task NR summary: applied rule IDs, actions, user benefits, evidence and unresolved checks. For a simple text task, a short factual summary suffices; no static scan or JSON record is required.

The portable nr_summary.py command validates a current task record and reruns three static checks: SQL projection, media autoplay and JavaScript polling. It does not authenticate declared evidence or verify all rules. An optional native hook checks summary structure and requests at most one correction. It requires explicit installation and trust review through Codex /hooks. It detects explicit $green-codex invocation, or a known rule ID or NR heading in the final answer; implicit use with none of these signals is not detected.

- [Closing summary format and command](https://github.com/Institut-du-Numerique-Responsable/green-codex/blob/main/green-codex/references/closing-summary.md)
- [Evaluation procedure and limits](https://github.com/Institut-du-Numerique-Responsable/green-codex/blob/main/evals/README.md)

## Example requests

- Review this collection endpoint. Check bounds and returned fields; cite tests and evidence gaps.
- Compare serverless and containers using our workload, latency and reliability requirements. Identify missing measurements before recommending a change.
- Review the affected accessibility requirements of this component. Distinguish automated findings from manual checks still needed.
- Compare AI solutions at equivalent task quality, including retries and tool use. Separate resource measurements from energy or carbon estimates.

No fixed percentage saving follows from a runtime, hosting model, cache or quantisation choice. Environmental claims need a baseline, workload, measurement boundary and uncertainty.

## Reuse

Code and scripts use Apache-2.0. Original documentation and rules use CC BY 4.0. The BP-AIR, stakeholder maturity and RIA31 adaptations use CC BY-SA 4.0, with attribution in each file. Reformulation does not remove licence duties. Opquast is a thematic reference, not an imported full checklist.

- [Licence scope](https://github.com/Institut-du-Numerique-Responsable/green-codex/blob/main/LICENSE)
- [Reuse rights](https://github.com/Institut-du-Numerique-Responsable/green-codex/blob/main/green-codex/references/reuse-rights.md)

Documentation is in English and French. Updates follow reviewed changes; no fixed monthly update schedule is promised.
